Published online:
August 21, 2026

Geographic focus:
South America (Brazil), West Africa (Ghana, Keta Basin), Africa broadly (Namibia, Ivory Coast, South Africa, São Tomé and Príncipe)

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical observation [NO]
T2. Forward-looking immediate [YES]
T3. Long-term development [YES]

Synopsis:
Petrobras has received approval from Ghana's Ministry of Energy to negotiate exploration contracts for four offshore blocks in the Keta Basin. The blocks are geologically comparable to Brazil's Equatorial Margin. This move is part of Petrobras' broader strategic pivot to make Africa its primary exploratory region outside Brazil, targeting reserve replenishment and long-term portfolio diversification across multiple African nations.

---

> Indirect and very long-horizon at best. Should Keta Basin exploration eventually yield LNG-exportable volumes, Europe could be a destination market — but this is speculative and many years away. No direct or near-term European market impact.
